newsitem.title: FINLAND: Some top names in Finland's "celebrity" Euro-poll.
newsitem.headline: Some top names in Finland's "celebrity" Euro-poll.

text.p: The focus is likely to be on personalities in Finland's European Parliament election on Sunday, featuring candidates ranging from political heavyweights to television personalities and a film maker.

The following alphabetically ordered sketches provide a glance at some of the 207 candidates vying for 16 seats in the Strasbourg-based parliament. Personality takes precedent over party affiliation in this selection.

- JORN DONNER, 63, author and film maker best-known for nude appearances in his avant-garde films, has said he is standing for the governing Social Democrats because he is fed up with his current consular position in Los Angeles. He has parliamentary experience and past links to two other parties.

JUHA FOHR, 38, a television weatherman running for the governing Swedish People's Party, sometimes presents his forecasts in leather and declared his homosexuality to a calm reception from viewers. He has served on Helsinki city council.

JAAKKO ILONIEMI, 64, is running for the opposition Progressive Finnish Party who in Finnish are called "Young Finns". He heads a Helsinki think-tank and has been ambassador to the United States and a banker. A highly regarded, outspoken commentator, he made a career as a Social Democrat but now runs for the smaller Progressives whose power-base is near Helsinki.

MARJO MATIKAINEN-KALLSTROM, 31, a former Olympic gold medallist in cross-country skiing is a Conservative with no political experience. Reporters' efforts to trip her up with tough questions seem not to have dented her popularity, which is based on her sporting achievements.

JYRKI OTILA, 55, standing as a Conservative, is a television quiz show host who has adopted the slogan, "Who knows best in the EU?". Among candidates questioned by the daily Aamulehti on their knowledge of European parliament affairs, he got one correct answer in six -- but they all fared poorly.

KIRSI PIHA, 29, a Conservative member of parliament seen as a big vote-puller for the governing National Coalition Party. Young, well-educated, international and attractive, she often features in tabloid papers and is seen as a natural politician.

ARJA SAIJONMAA, 51, a popular singer running for the Swedish People's Party, has been a goodwill ambassador for the United Nations. She made a name mainly in Sweden and with Greek folk music composer Mikis Theodorakis. She belonged to the leftist cultural fringe in the 1960s.

PAAVO VAYRYNEN, 50, is a heavyweight member of parliament for the opposition Centre Party, and his party's top Euro-sceptic. A former foreign minister, party leader and twice presidential candidate, his stance on Europe has put him at odds with the party's power brokers.
MATTI WUORI, 50, a lawyer running for the Green Party, is head of Finnish Greenpeace and former chairman of international Greenpeace. He makes a campaigning point of saying he is not a politician.
